extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners (and their counsel), USPTO Office of Enrollment & Discipline staff, and other USPTO stakeholders
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and conditions governing approval of an Affidavit of Resignation under 37 C.F.R. § 11.27 and the resulting exclusion on consent, including required acknowledgements in the affidavit and post-exclusion obligations (limited recognition, account prohibitions, reinstatement rules).

rubrics_metrics.name: Affidavit of Resignation must comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.27(a)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent's Affidavit of Resignation must comply with the requirements of 37 C.F.R. § 11.27(a) for an exclusion on consent to be approved by the USPTO Director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order states: 'Respondent's Affidavit of Resignation complies with the requirements of 37 C.F.R. § 11.27(a). Accordingly, it is hereby ORDERED that: Respondent's Affidavit of Resignation shall be, and hereby is, approved.' Compliance is the precondition for approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voluntary consent — no coercion or duress
rubrics_metrics.description: The affidavit must state that the respondent's consent to exclusion is freely and voluntarily rendered and that the respondent is not being subjected to coercion or duress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affidavit item 1: 'His consent is freely and voluntarily rendered, and he is not being subjected to coercion or duress.' This is a required factual representation in the affidavit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Awareness of pending OED investigation and disclosed allegations
rubrics_metrics.description: The respondent must acknowledge awareness that the OED Director opened an investigation and of the allegations/information obtained in that investigation (state discipline, suspensions, admonitions, grievance allegations, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affidavit item 2: respondent acknowledges awareness of OED File No. 04628 and the information obtained (e.g., administrative suspension in California for failure to pay child support, Arizona admonition with probation and costs, later grievance alleging continued failures to pay support). The Final Order recites these facts as the basis for the OED opinion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledgement of OED Director's opinion of violation (37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: The affidavit (or order) should reflect that the respondent is aware the OED Director is of the opinion that the respondent violated at least 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h)(1) (being publicly disciplined on ethical or professional misconduct grounds by a duly constituted authority of a State).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affidavit item 3: 'He is aware that the OED Director is of the opinion ... that he violated at least 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h)(1).' The Order relies on that opinion as part of the investigative background.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-admission with presumption for reinstatement
rubrics_metrics.description: A respondent may not admit the USPTO disciplinary rule violations in the pending investigation but must acknowledge that, for purposes of any future reinstatement under 37 C.F.R. § 11.60, the OED Director will conclusively presume the investigation facts are true and that the respondent could not have successfully defended against the OED Director's opinion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affidavit item 4: respondent 'Without admitting to violating any ... rules ... acknowledges that ... the OED Director will conclusively presume ... (a) the facts ... are true, and (b) he could not have successfully defended himself against the allegations ...' This limits future factual dispute on reinstatement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affiant must understand relevant regulations and legal consequences (§§ 11.5(b), 11.27, 11.58, 11.59, 11.60)
rubrics_metrics.description: The affidavit must affirm that the respondent has fully read and understands the specified USPTO Rules (including §§ 11.5(b), 11.27, 11.58, 11.59, and 11.60) and is aware of the legal and factual consequences of consenting to exclusion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affidavit item 5: explicit acknowledgement of reading and understanding the listed regulations and consequences is a required element for approval of the resignation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consent to exclusion from practice before the USPTO
rubrics_metrics.description: The respondent must expressly consent to being excluded from practice before the USPTO in patent, trademark, and other non-patent matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affidavit item 6: 'He consents to being excluded from practice before the USPTO in patent, trademark, and other non-patent matters.' This is the substantive act effecting exclusion on consent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited recognition for 30 days to conclude pending matters (§ 11.58(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon approval of an affidavit of resignation, the respondent may be granted limited recognition for a 30‑day period commencing on the Final Order date to conclude work on behalf of any clients on matters pending before the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Order item 3: 'Respondent is hereby granted limited recognition for a period of thirty (30) days ... to conclude work on behalf of a client on any matters pending before the Office; and, if such work cannot be concluded, Respondent shall so advise the client so that the client may make other arrangements.' The respondent must comply with § 11.58 during this period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of Final Order in OED FOIA Reading Room and Official Gazette
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall electronically publish the Final Order in the Office of Enrollment and Discipline's FOIA Reading Room and publish a notice in the Official Gazette materially consistent with the provided sample notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Order items 4 and 5: explicit publication directives and a sample 'Notice of Exclusion on Consent' are provided, including the factual matters to be publicized (registration number, reasons, state discipline summary, admonition/probation, and presumption language).

rubrics_metrics.name: Full compliance with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58 obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: The respondent shall comply fully with the requirements of 37 C.F.R. § 11.58 (rules governing suspension/exclusion obligations, client notification, handling of files, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Order item 6: 'Respondent shall comply fully with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58.' The Final Order ties limited recognition and post-exclusion responsibilities to § 11.58 compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: USPTO.gov account restrictions and authority to disable/suspend accounts
rubrics_metrics.description: Effective after expiration of the 30‑day limited recognition, USPTO is authorized to disable or suspend any USPTO.gov accounts registered to the respondent; respondent is prohibited from applying for, obtaining, verifying, sponsoring, or otherwise assisting with USPTO verified Electronic System accounts until reinstated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Order items 7–10: specific prohibitions include: not applying for a USPTO verified Electronic System account; not obtaining or having name added to such accounts; not verifying others' credentials; not sponsoring accounts. The USPTO may disable or suspend accounts; respondent cannot use USPTO systems to prepare/file documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respondent bears responsibility to seek re-activation of disabled accounts
rubrics_metrics.description: The Final Order does not obligate the USPTO to re-activate any disabled or suspended USPTO.gov accounts; it is the respondent's sole responsibility to initiate any such re-activation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Order item 11: clarifies that after accounts are disabled/suspended, the USPTO need not act sua sponte and the respondent must pursue reactivation if desired.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to comply with reinstatement procedures under 37 C.F.R. § 11.60
rubrics_metrics.description: Until a petition for reinstatement is granted under 37 C.F.R. § 11.60, the respondent remains prohibited from practice; upon any request for reinstatement, the respondent must comply fully with § 11.60.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Order item 12: 'Respondent shall comply fully with 37 C.F.R. § 11.60 upon any request for reinstatement.' Also tied to the presumption language in the affidavit regarding how OED will treat facts on reinstatement.

rubrics_metrics.name: State public discipline constitutes grounds under 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h)(1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Being publicly disciplined on ethical or professional misconduct grounds by a duly constituted authority of a State is identified as a ground or predicate matter relevant to USPTO professional conduct rules (cited as 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h)(1)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order references the California administrative suspension and the Arizona admonition/probation as the types of state disciplinary actions that form the basis for the OED Director's opinion and for the respondent's acknowledgement under the affidavit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sample Official Gazette notice content must include material facts
rubrics_metrics.description: The Official Gazette notice must be materially consistent with the provided sample, including registration number, voluntary submission during a pending disciplinary investigation, state discipline summary, admonition/probation details, and the presumption language about reinstatement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Order item 5 includes a 'Notice of Exclusion on Consent' sample text specifying what facts and acknowledgements should be publicly reported; the Gazette notice must be materially consistent with that sample.

rubrics_metrics.name: USPTO Director's statutory authority to approve exclusion on consent
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director's authority to approve an affidavit of resignation and exclude a practitioner on consent derives from 35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 32 and 37 C.F.R. § 11.27.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order cites statutory/regulatory authority (35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 32; 37 C.F.R. § 11.27) to justify approval and issuance of the exclusion order; this is the legal basis for processing and evaluating affidavits of resignation.
